read.bigIdea: American whiskey is named by its grain.
read.where: Whiskey is distilled from a **grain mash** and aged in **oak**. **Bourbon, rye, wheat and malt whiskey** each need **at least 51%** of that grain, distilling at **160 proof or less**, and aging in **new charred oak** barrels, entered at 125 proof or less. **Corn whiskey** needs at least **80% corn** and doesn’t need new charred oak. It’s all bottled at **80 proof or more**.

keyPoints.line: only: bourbon is made in the United States.
Kentucky: any state can make bourbon.
bourbons are softer; high-rye are spicier.

read.bigIdea: American, at least 51% corn, new charred oak.
read.where: **Bourbon** must be made in the **United States**, but **not only in Kentucky**. Corn gives it sweetness. The other grains change the taste: **wheated** bourbons swap rye for wheat and taste softer; **high-rye** bourbons are spicier. **Small batch** and **single barrel** aren’t defined in the federal rules: they’re the maker’s own words.

stops.name: Small batch
stops.text: A blend of a few barrels; the maker’s term.

read.mixup: **Bourbon** can come from any US state. Kentucky makes most of it.
read.sayIt: Bourbon is a little sweeter; rye is a little spicier.

keyPoints.line: means at least two years in new charred oak.
means one distiller, one season, four years.

read.bigIdea: Two label words that are rules, not marketing.
read.where: **Straight** whiskey has aged at least **two years** in new charred oak. **Bottled-in-bond** goes further: made by **one distiller** in **one distilling season**, aged at least **four years** in a government-bonded warehouse, and bottled at exactly **100 proof**. The rule dates to **1897**.

keyPoints.line: is spicier and drier than bourbon.
whiskey is filtered through maple charcoal first.
Process is the name for that charcoal step.

read.bigIdea: Spicy rye, and Tennessee’s charcoal step.
read.where: **Rye whiskey** is at least 51% rye, so it’s **spicier and drier** than bourbon. **Tennessee whiskey**, by a 2013 state law, follows the bourbon rules and is also **filtered through maple charcoal** before it goes into the barrel: the **Lincoln County Process**. Jack Daniel’s is the best-known example.

keyPoints.line: is bourbon, Campari and sweet vermouth.
is rye with absinthe and Peychaud’s.

read.where: The **Old Fashioned**, **Manhattan** (whiskey and sweet vermouth) and **Whiskey Sour** take bourbon or rye. The **Sazerac** is rye with absinthe and Peychaud’s. The **Boulevardier** is bourbon, Campari and sweet vermouth. The **Mint Julep** is bourbon, mint and sugar over crushed ice. The **Gold Rush** is bourbon, lemon and honey.
